episodes.title: The missed move — Nov 3-4, 2026 (the +95pt rally the engine stayed bearish through)
justification: Ensemble forecast for the 2026-11-03 17:00Z bar: 24h up-rank 85.1485, journaled 2026-11-03T18:51:56Z in restart catch-up (forecast record, D1 cadence, alert_fired).
Its 12h reconciliation (journaled 2026-11-04T07:00:10Z): run_up +95.35pts, ret +2.395% — the rally was real and the forecast called it.

Live posture stayed bearish: judgment_thesis records show bearish thesis created 13:00Z, maintained 13:30Z, then re-created fresh at 15:00Z and 16:00Z by restarted runs — never weakened, never invalidated.
Hot Scalp armed 232 setups in-window and blocked 87 candidates on geometry.net_rr_below_min (121 across Nov 3-4).
Judgment shadow TOOK the 2026-11-04 06:00Z order_block short (expected_r +0.7287); reconciliations graded it -1.8647R (08:00Z) and -2.7504R (11:00Z).

residuals: Assessment-stream discontinuity: the live journal's judgment assessments stop at 16:00Z on Nov 3 (restarts re-created the thesis per run; Nov 4 runs journaled no thesis records at all). WS1's revision machinery can only revise on assessments it receives — in replay, thesis-1 is invalidated at 15:00Z and the same update creates its scenario-only successor (maintained at 16:00Z), which is still the active thesis at the 06:00Z scan; the gate therefore adopts the thesis-aligned order_block short as a child (verdict: child), and what ends that setup is WS3's close-rule invalidation before any trigger fire — not the gate. The fix this points at is keeper persistence / assessment continuity across restarts, which is outside WS1's shipped scope.

The handoff leg's instances carry thesis_id null: that leg runs the sweep path without judgment cycles, so no keeper adoption resolves there. Thesis-link stamping on scan instances is pinned by WS3's own suite (test_scan_instance_stamped_with_parent_thesis) and the keeper-side adoption is demonstrated in this replay's thesis leg (thesis_child_registered at 13:00Z, cut by thesis_orphaned at 15:00Z).

Weakening is not exercised by this episode's tape: at the 15:00Z cycle the price fact (3944.595 at/above the thesis's own invalidation price 3944.42) closes the thesis structurally in the same update that carries the erosion (winner_p peak 0.7568 -> 0.5337), and invalidation is checked before revision. The weakening path itself is pinned by WS1's own suite; no recorded assessment in this journal erodes a surviving thesis without also breaking it.

Trigger binding, traced to the record (follow-up to this battery): the window's 25 __trigger__ evaluations decompose as 11 zone-touch armings + 8 left-zone invalidations of the trigger machine's own pendings — records that never reach the lifecycle binder by construction — plus 3 fires with their 3 execution dispositions.  All three fires were SHORT (01:30Z and 01:43Z volume_spike, 05:30Z failed_retest, against the bearish live setup at ~3955), and at each the binder's same-direction group was empty: the only armed instances were the inversion LONGS (the 20:00Z and 23:00Z touches), the one earlier short instance (17:00Z touch) had expired at 23:00Z on Nov 3, and the next short (order_block) registered at 06:00Z, after the last fire — each fire's own disposition record confirms 'armed setups remaining in direction: 0'.  The 02:00Z tape mark (3947.047) crossing the long's target is a reconciliation price fact, not a trigger event: a scan instance's target is an exit level, and routing binds on same-direction trigger FIRES, of which no long fire occurred in the instance's life.  Non-binding was therefore correct behavior, not a binder defect; the bracket / nearest / oldest selection never had a same-direction group to select from.  The gap the trace exposed was evidentiary, and it is closed: every fire that reaches the selection now journals one kind=trigger_binding record — the bound instance and its rule, or the not-bound reason (no_armed_instances / direction_mismatch / all_expired / shadow_only) with every armed instance's disposition — so a future episode reads its answer off one record instead of a forensic pass.  Capture of that long is still not claimed: no long trigger fire existed to capture it with.

The forecast was operationally available for ~11.1h before the 06:00Z scan and the system's posture never moved: E3 keeps forecasts journal-only until live calibration earns weight (top-band lift >= 1.25, >= 20 resolutions), so this is doctrine operating as designed, recorded here as the standing tension the owner's calibration program has to resolve — not a WS1-WS3 defect.

Hot Scalp repricing is exhibit-deep, not census-deep: the journal's blocked-candidate records carry risk / reward / net_rr but not the M5 structure the current planner prices from, so the other geometry-blocked setups of the window cannot be re-priced without inventing bars. The two exhibits are the episode's journal-exact representatives (one each way); the census (87 blocks in-window, 78 of them longs) is reported as journal fact.
